## 1. LOAD PACKAGES

```{r load-packages}
library(janitor)      # column name cleaning
library(dplyr)        # data manipulation
library(tidyr)        # data reshaping
library(ggplot2)      # visualisation
library(lme4)         # mixed-effects models
library(lmerTest)     # p-values for lmer
library(emmeans)      # estimated marginal means
library(performance)  # ICC
library(see)      # for model check
```

---

## 2. LOAD AND CLEAN DATA

```{r load-data}
# Read raw data and clean column names
data <- read.csv("microCT_measurements_all.csv", header = TRUE) %>%
  clean_names()

# Quick inspection of dataset structure
str(data)
head(data)
summary(data)

# Ensure Feret diameter is numeric
data$feret_micron <- as.numeric(data$feret_micron)

# SUBSET GAMETE DATA ONLY
# Keep only gamete-related measurements (exclude tissue classes like mesohyl/spicules)
gametes <- data %>%
  filter(grepl("Gamete", type, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !is.na(feret_micron))

# Add phylum column for broad taxonomic comparisons
gametes <- gametes %>%
  mutate(
    phylum = ifelse(species == "Paragorgia arborea",
                    "Cnidaria",
                    "Porifera")
  )
```

---

## 3. DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY

```{r descriptive-summary}
# Total gametes measured per method
gametes %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_feret = mean(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_feret = sd(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Raw Feret distributions by method and stage
ggplot(gametes, aes(x = method, y = feret_micron)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ stage, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Method", y = "Feret diameter (µm)")


```

## 4. DETECTION LIMIT

```{r detection-limit}
# ---- 5a. MicroCT detection limits ----
# Overall minimum
microCT_limit <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "microCT") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(microCT_limit)

# By phylum
microCT_limit_sponges <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "microCT", phylum == "Porifera") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(microCT_limit_sponges)

microCT_limit_cnidaria <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "microCT", phylum == "Cnidaria") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(microCT_limit_cnidaria)

# ---- 5b. Histology detection limits ----
histo_limit <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "histology") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(histo_limit)

histo_limit_sponges <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "histology", phylum == "Porifera") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(histo_limit_sponges)

histo_limit_cnidaria <- gametes %>%
  filter(method == "histology", phylum == "Cnidaria") %>%
  summarise(min_detected = min(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE))
print(histo_limit_cnidaria)
```

## 5. GAMETE COUNTS

```{r gamete-counts}

# ---- 4a. Total counts per specimen and method ----
counts_table <- gametes %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, method) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

print(counts_table)

# Bar plot: counts per specimen
ggplot(counts_table, aes(x = specimen_id)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = microCT, fill = "microCT"), position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = histology, fill = "histology"), position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  labs(y = "Number of gametes counted", x = "Specimen", fill = "Method") +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("microCT" = "#1b9e77", "histology" = "#d95f02"))

# ---- 4b. Counts by stage (stacked) ----
counts_stage <- gametes %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, method, stage) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Create a combined label for x-axis 
counts_stage <- counts_stage %>%
  mutate(specimen_method = paste(specimen_id, method, sep = "."))

ggplot(counts_stage, aes(x = specimen_method, y = n, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Specimen / method",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Stage"
  ) 

# No stats between bars because I then only compare two numbers... I could group the species and then compare the three replicates... 

# ---- 4c. Ratio of microCT to histology counts ----
counts_table <- counts_table %>%
  mutate(ratio = ifelse(histology > 0, microCT / histology, NA))

counts_table %>%
  dplyr::select(specimen_id, microCT, histology, ratio) %>%
  print()

# Test if normal distribution or not: normality test (if p is below 0.05 then not non-parametric)
shapiro.test(counts_table$microCT) # = not normal
shapiro.test(counts_table$histology) # = not normal 

# ---- 4d. Paired statistical tests on counts ----
# Wilcoxon signed-rank test (non-parametric, robust to outliers)
wilcox.test(counts_table$microCT, counts_table$histology, paired = TRUE)

# ---- 4e. Phylum-specific count comparison ----
# Join phylum info to counts_table
counts_table <- counts_table %>%
  left_join(
    gametes %>% dplyr::select(specimen_id, phylum) %>% distinct(),
    by = "specimen_id"
  )

# Split into phyla and test
counts_porifera <- counts_table %>% filter(phylum == "Porifera")
counts_cnidaria <- counts_table %>% filter(phylum == "Cnidaria")

# Wilcoxon tests for each phylum
print("Porifera counts (microCT vs histology):")
wilcox.test(counts_porifera$microCT, counts_porifera$histology, paired = TRUE)

print("Cnidaria counts (microCT vs histology):")
wilcox.test(counts_cnidaria$microCT, counts_cnidaria$histology, paired = TRUE) #only three samples/numbers, so obviously not significant... 

```


## 6. COMPARE COUNTS (>70 µm DETECTION THRESHOLD)

```{r counts-filtered}

# ---- 6a. Filter ----
gametes_large <- gametes %>% filter(feret_micron > 70)

counts_large <- gametes_large %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, method) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    ratio = ifelse(histology > 0, microCT / histology, NA)
  ) %>%
  # Add phylum for grouping
  left_join(
    gametes %>% dplyr::select(specimen_id, phylum, species) %>% distinct(),
    by = "specimen_id"
  )

print(counts_large)

# ---- 6b. Statistical tests ----
# Overall (all taxa)
p_global <- wilcox.test(counts_large$microCT, counts_large$histology, paired = TRUE)$p.value
p_label_global <- ifelse(p_global < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(p_global, 3)))

# Sponges only
counts_large_sponges <- counts_large %>% filter(phylum == "Porifera")
p_sponges <- t.test(counts_large_sponges$microCT, counts_large_sponges$histology, paired = TRUE)$p.value
p_label_sponges <- ifelse(p_sponges < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste0("p = ", round(p_sponges, 3)))

# Paragorgia only (ratio, no p-value due to n=3)
counts_large_coral <- counts_large %>% filter(phylum == "Cnidaria")
mean_ratio_coral <- mean(counts_large_coral$ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

# ---- 6c. Publication-ready bar plot with annotations ----
# Reshape for plotting
counts_large_plot <- counts_large %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(histology, microCT),
               names_to = "method",
               values_to = "n")

# Determine max value for annotation placement
max_n <- max(counts_large_plot$n, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(counts_large_plot, aes(x = specimen_id, y = n, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
  # Add overall significance annotation
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, 
           label = paste0("Overall: microCT > histology\n", p_label_global),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
  # Add sponges p-value
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max_n * 1.15, 
           label = paste0("Sponges: p = ", round(p_sponges, 3)),
           size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
  # Add Paragorgia ratio
  annotate("text", x = 10.5, y = max_n * 1.15, 
           label = paste0("Paragorgia: ratio = ", round(mean_ratio_coral, 2), "×"),
           size = 3.5, fontface = "italic") +
  # Add dashed lines to separate phyla (optional)
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(3.5, 6.5, 9.5), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Add phylum labels
  annotate("text", x = 2, y = max_n * 1.25, 
           label = "Sponges (n=9)", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = 10.5, y = max_n * 1.25, 
           label = "Paragorgia (n=3)", fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Specimen", 
    y = "Number of gametes >70 µm",
    fill = "Method",
    caption = "Dashed lines separate phyla. Overall comparison: Wilcoxon signed-rank test.\nSponges: paired t-test. Paragorgia: n=3, ratio shown instead of p-value."
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# ---- Filtered counts by stage (stacked) ----
# Use gametes_large (already filtered to >70 µm)
counts_stage_filtered <- gametes_large %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, method, stage) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Create a combined label for x-axis
counts_stage_filtered <- counts_stage_filtered %>%
  mutate(specimen_method = paste(specimen_id, method, sep = "."))

# Stacked bar plot
ggplot(counts_stage_filtered, aes(x = specimen_method, y = n, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Specimen / method",
    y = "Count (gametes >70 µm)",
    fill = "Stage"
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Stage")

# ---- 6d. Sponge-only tests on filtered counts ----
# Subset to Porifera only
counts_large_porifera <- counts_large %>% filter(phylum == "Porifera")

shapiro.test(counts_large_porifera$microCT) #not normal so use Wilcox
shapiro.test(counts_large_porifera$histology) #not normal so use Wilcox 

#Wilcox paired test (non parametric)
wilcox_test_sponges <- wilcox.test(counts_large_porifera$microCT, 
                                   counts_large_porifera$histology, 
                                   paired = TRUE)
print(wilcox_test_sponges)

# Paired t-test (parametric, robust with n=9) - just to check if it fits with Wilcox test, 
t_test_sponges <- t.test(counts_large_porifera$microCT, 
                         counts_large_porifera$histology, 
                         paired = TRUE)
print(t_test_sponges)

# ---- View ratios from filtered data ----
counts_large %>%
  dplyr::select(specimen_id, phylum, species, histology, microCT, ratio) %>%
  arrange(phylum, desc(ratio)) %>%
  print()

```

## 7. PAIRED COMPARISON: SPECIMEN × STAGE × METHOD MEANS

```{r aggregate-means}
# Aggregate to specimen × stage × method means
# This is the unit of analysis for paired comparisons
specimen_stage <- gametes %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, species, phylum, stage, method) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_feret = mean(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_feret = median(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_feret = sd(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

---

## 8. UNFILTERED ANALYSIS (MAIN MODEL)

```{r unfiltered-analysis}

# ---- 8a. Bland-Altman (unfiltered) ----

paired_raw <- specimen_stage %>%
  dplyr::select(specimen_id, species, stage, method, mean_feret) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = mean_feret) %>%
  filter(!is.na(microCT) & !is.na(histology)) %>%
  mutate(diff = microCT - histology,
         mean = (microCT + histology) / 2)

# Bland-Altman plot - this is to see how the methods differ. 
ggplot(paired_raw, aes(x = mean, y = diff)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff), linetype = "solid", color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff) + 1.96 * sd(paired_raw$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff) - 1.96 * sd(paired_raw$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mean feret (µm)", y = "Difference (microCT - histology)") +
  theme_bw()

# Proportional bias test (unfiltered)
prop_bias <- lm(diff ~ mean, data = paired_raw) #fitting a linear regression (response = diff, microCT vs histo // predictor = mean)
summary(prop_bias) # This tests whether the difference between methods changes with the size of the measurement – i.e., whether the bias is proportional to the magnitude of the measurement.

# Visualise the proportional bias: Bland-Altman plot with proportional bias line
ggplot(paired_raw, aes(x = mean, y = diff)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff), linetype = "solid", color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff) + 1.96 * sd(paired_raw$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_raw$diff) - 1.96 * sd(paired_raw$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "darkgreen", linetype = "dotted") +  # <-- ADD THIS
  labs(x = "Mean feret (µm)", y = "Difference (microCT - histology)") +
  theme_bw()


# ---- Bland-Altman summary statistics ----
mean_diff <- mean(paired_raw$diff, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_diff <- sd(paired_raw$diff, na.rm = TRUE)
loa_lower <- mean_diff - 1.96 * sd_diff
loa_upper <- mean_diff + 1.96 * sd_diff

cat("Mean difference (microCT - histology):", round(mean_diff, 1), "µm\n")
cat("SD of differences:", round(sd_diff, 1), "µm\n")
cat("95% limits of agreement: [", round(loa_lower, 1), ",", round(loa_upper, 1), "] µm\n")


# ---- 8b. Mixed-effects model (unfiltered) ---- MAIN MODEL

# Main model = liear mixed effects model (method × stage interaction with random intercept per specimen)
# This tests: Main effect of method: Are microCT measurements systematically different from histology? Main effect of stage: Do # gamete sizes differ across developmental stages? PLus Interaction (method × stage): Does the method difference vary by stage?

model4 <- lmer(feret_micron ~ method * stage + (1 | specimen_id), data = gametes) #The random intercept (1 | specimen_id) accounts for the fact that multiple gametes come from the same specimen.
summary(model4)

anova(model4, type = 3) #type 3 because it tests each term after all otheer terms, including the interactions (so this needs to be used when interactions are present). Here we test the method vs stage (method:stage = The method difference varies significantly by stage...)

```

# STAGE SPECIFIC CONTRASTS (UNFILTERED DATA)
```{r}

# ---- 8c. Estimated marginal means and pairwise contrasts for stages ----
# This is a post-hoc pairwise comparison – the stage‑specific contrasts that form the core of the stage‑specific results 

emm_raw <- emmeans(model4, ~ method | stage)
contrasts_raw <- contrast(emm_raw, "pairwise", by = "stage", adjust = "tukey")
print(contrasts_raw)

# ---- Improved boxplot by stage with significance stars ----
# Extract significance from contrasts_raw
sig_data <- as.data.frame(contrasts_raw)
sig_data <- sig_data %>%
  mutate(
    star = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    ),
    # Calculate y position for stars (max Feret per stage + some offset)
    y_pos = gametes %>%
      group_by(stage) %>%
      summarise(max_feret = max(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      pull(max_feret) * 1.05
  )

# Plot
ggplot(gametes, aes(x = method, y = feret_micron, fill = method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +  # hide outliers for cleaner look
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2), 
             aes(color = method), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ stage, scales = "free_y") +
  # Add significance stars
  geom_text(data = sig_data %>% filter(star != "ns"),
            aes(x = 1.5, y = y_pos, label = star),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5, vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Method", y = "Feret diameter (µm)", 
       title = "Size distributions by developmental stage")


# ---- 8d. Model diagnostics ----
plot(model4)          # residuals vs fitted
qqnorm(resid(model4)); qqline(resid(model4))

```

## 9. FILTERED ANALYSIS: FILTERED TO >70 µm

```{r filtered-analysis}

### Do the same as above, but with the filtered data 

# ---- Combined stages with filtered data ----

# Step 1: Recode stages into combined categories
gametes_filtered <- gametes %>%
  filter(feret_micron > 70) %>%
  mutate(
    stage_combined = case_when(
      # Combine vitellogenic oocyte + late oocyte/early embryo (for sponges, since it was difficult to determine them, and makes it comparable to Paragorgia)
      stage %in% c("vitellogenic oocyte", "late oocyte or early embryo") ~ "Vitellogenic / late oocyte",
      # Combine prelarva + larva (same, difficult to draw a line...)
      stage %in% c("prelarva", "larva") ~ "Larva / prelarva",
      # Keep others as is
      TRUE ~ stage
    )
  )

# Step 2: Refit mixed model with combined stages (= make stats matching)
# This is optional but recommended if the significance of stars should reflect the combined categories
model_combined <- lmer(feret_micron ~ method * stage_combined + (1 | specimen_id),
                       data = gametes_filtered)
summary(model_combined)
anova(model_combined, type = 3)

# Step 3: Get contrasts for combined stages
emm_combined <- emmeans(model_combined, ~ method | stage_combined)
contrasts_combined <- contrast(emm_combined, "pairwise", by = "stage_combined", adjust = "tukey")
print(contrasts_combined)

# Step 4: Prepare significance stars for the plot
sig_data_combined <- as.data.frame(contrasts_combined)
sig_data_combined <- sig_data_combined %>%
  mutate(
    star = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Get y-position for stars
  left_join(
    gametes_filtered %>%
      group_by(stage_combined) %>%
      summarise(max_feret = max(feret_micron, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "stage_combined"
  ) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = max_feret * 1.05)

# Step 5: Plot
ggplot(gametes_filtered, aes(x = method, y = feret_micron, fill = method)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2), 
             aes(color = method), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ stage_combined, scales = "free_y") +
  # Add significance stars
  geom_text(data = sig_data_combined %>% filter(star != "ns"),
            aes(x = 1.5, y = y_pos, label = star),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 5, vjust = 0) +
  # Add "ns" for non‑significant stages
  geom_text(data = sig_data_combined %>% filter(star == "ns"),
            aes(x = 1.5, y = y_pos, label = "ns"),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4, vjust = 0, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Method", y = "Feret diameter (µm)", 
       title = "Size distributions by combined developmental stage (gametes >70 µm)")


##########


# ---- 9a. Filter aggregated means ----
common <- specimen_stage %>%
  filter(mean_feret > 70) %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, stage) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>%  # keep only stages present in both methods
  ungroup()

# ---- 9b. Bland-Altman (filtered) ----
paired_filtered <- common %>%
  dplyr::select(specimen_id, species, stage, method, mean_feret) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = mean_feret) %>%
  filter(!is.na(microCT) & !is.na(histology)) %>%
  mutate(diff = microCT - histology,
         mean = (microCT + histology) / 2)

ggplot(paired_filtered, aes(x = mean, y = diff)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_filtered$diff), linetype = "solid", color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_filtered$diff) + 1.96 * sd(paired_filtered$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(paired_filtered$diff) - 1.96 * sd(paired_filtered$diff),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mean feret (µm)", y = "Difference (microCT - histology)") +
  theme_bw()

prop_bias_filt <- lm(diff ~ mean, data = paired_filtered)
summary(prop_bias_filt) # similar to unfiltered data, so still true (signficant)

# ---- 9c. Mixed-effects model (filtered) ----
# This is a sensitivity analysis using specimen-stage means (not individual gametes).
# The stage interaction is not significant, confirming that size-filtering removes
# the stage dependence observed in the unfiltered model.
m2 <- lmer(mean_feret ~ method * stage + (1 | specimen_id),
           data = common)
summary(m2)
anova(m2, type = 3)

# ---- 9d. Weighted version (by number of gametes per mean) ----
# Weight by number of gametes per mean; results are consistent with unweighted model.

m2_weighted <- lmer(mean_feret ~ method * stage + (1 | specimen_id),
                    data = common, weights = n)
summary(m2_weighted)

# ---- 9e. Effect sizes and percentage bias ----

# We are using emmeans, because this uses the model to predict what the mean would be for each stage‑method combination, adjusted for the random effects (specimen variation) and balanced across stages. This gives a fair comparison that accounts for the hierarchical structure of your data. If only raw means, then it doesnt account for differences in sample sizes... mean will be influenced by sample size... 


common <- common %>%
  mutate(
    stage_combined = case_when(
      stage %in% c("vitellogenic oocyte", "late oocyte or early embryo") ~ "Vitellogenic / late oocyte",
      stage %in% c("prelarva", "larva") ~ "Larva / prelarva",
      TRUE ~ as.character(stage)
    ),
    stage_combined = factor(stage_combined,
                            levels = c("previtellogenic oocyte",
                                       "Vitellogenic / late oocyte",
                                       "embryo",
                                       "Larva / prelarva"))
  )
#reaggregate because somehow I got duplicates above...
common <- common %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, species, stage_combined, method) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_feret = mean(mean_feret),
    n = sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(specimen_id, stage_combined) %>%
  filter(n() == 2) %>%     # keep only stage-specimen combos in both methods
  ungroup()

# Sanity check: should return zero rows
common %>%
  dplyr::count(specimen_id, stage_combined, method) %>%
  filter(n > 1)


m2_combined <- lmer(mean_feret ~ method * stage_combined + (1 | specimen_id),
                    data = common)
anova(m2_combined, type = 3)
summary(m2_combined)

emm_m2c <- emmeans(m2_combined, ~ method | stage_combined)  # Computes the estimated marginal means (model‑predicted averages) for each method within each stage from the filtered model (m2).
contrasts_m2c <- contrast(emm_m2c, "pairwise", by = "stage_combined") #Compares the two methods (histology vs microCT) separately for each stage. The contrast is histology - microCT (so a negative estimate means microCT is larger).
summary(contrasts_m2c, by = NULL, adjust = "holm")


hist_means <- as.data.frame(emm_m2c) %>%
  filter(method == "histology") %>%
  dplyr::select(stage_combined, hist_mean = emmean)

#

# ---- 9f. Model diagnostics for filtered model ----
plot(m2)          # residuals vs fitted
qqnorm(resid(m2))
qqline(resid(m2))



# On combined stages:

# Histology emmeans
hist_em <- as.data.frame(emm_combined) %>%
  filter(method == "histology") %>%
  dplyr::select(stage_combined, hist_mean = emmean)

# Contrasts (histology - microCT)
contr <- as.data.frame(contrasts_combined) %>%
  mutate(microCT_minus_histology = -estimate)  # positive = microCT larger

# Join and compute percent bias
pct_table <- left_join(contr, hist_em, by = "stage_combined") %>%
  mutate(percent_bias = (microCT_minus_histology / hist_mean) * 100) %>%
  dplyr::select(stage_combined, contrast_est = estimate, hist_mean, 
                microCT_minus_histology, percent_bias)
pct_table

# Overall marginal means averaged over stages
emm_all <- emmeans(model_combined, ~ method)
emm_tab <- as.data.frame(emm_all)
(overall_pct <- (emm_tab$emmean[2] - emm_tab$emmean[1]) / emm_tab$emmean[1] * 100)
pairs(emm_all)
```

# 10. SPECIES AND PHYLUM EFFECTS

```{r species-phylum-effects}

# ---- 10a. Species as a fixed effect ----
# Check how the species differed, so adding species into the linear mixed effects model: 

model_species <- lmer(feret_micron ~ method * species + stage + (1 | specimen_id),
                      data = gametes)
summary(model_species)
anova(model_species, type = 3)

# ---- Pairwise contrasts per species ----
# Use unweighted emmeans for contrasts (the differences are the same)
emm_species <- emmeans(model_species, ~ method | species)
contrasts_species <- contrast(emm_species, "pairwise", by = "species", adjust = "tukey")
print(contrasts_species)

# ---- Species-specific means with weighted emmeans ----
# Use weights = "cells" to average only over stages that exist in each species.
# This prevents the model from extrapolating to stages that are absent (e.g., 
# prelarva and late oocyte/early embryo in Paragorgia).
emm_species_weighted <- emmeans(model_species, ~ method | species, weights = "cells")
emm_species_df <- as.data.frame(emm_species_weighted)

# ---- Annotation: significance stars ----
# All pairwise contrasts are significant (p < 0.001), so we place "***" above each species.
annotation_species <- emm_species_df %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    y_star = max(upper.CL) + 30,  # 30 µm above the highest error bar
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ---- Publication-ready species plot ----
ggplot(emm_species_df, aes(x = species, y = emmean, color = method)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(0.2), size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                position = position_dodge(0.2), width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Significance stars
  geom_text(data = annotation_species,
            aes(x = species, y = y_star, label = "***"),
            color = "black", size = 5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("histology" = "#d95f02", "microCT" = "#1b9e77"),
                     name = "Method") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position = "top"
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Estimated mean Feret diameter (µm)",
    x = "Species",
    caption = "*** p < 0.001 for histology vs. microCT within each species (Tukey-adjusted).\nMeans are weighted estimated marginal means (emmeans) adjusted for developmental stage,\nweighted by the observed stage distribution per species (stages absent from a species are excluded)."
  )

# ---- 10b. Phylum effects ----
model_group <- lmer(feret_micron ~ method * phylum * stage + (1 | specimen_id),
                    data = gametes)
summary(model_group)
anova(model_group)

model_phylum <- lmer(feret_micron ~ method * phylum + (1 | specimen_id),
                     data = gametes)
summary(model_phylum)
anova(model_phylum)
```

(ICC) - maybe not needed, since I have too few specimens

```{r icc}

#Using ICC = Intraclass Correlation Coefficient Analysis
#Can say how much of the total variation in gamete size is due to differences between specimens (as opposed to variation within specimens, e.g., between stages or measurement error). ICC measures clustering – how similar measurements are within the same specimen compared to measurements from different specimens.
# So 0 = no variation, all specimens are identical
# If ICC > 0.5 then high, specimens are very different from eachother

# ---- 11a. ICC for filtered model ----
icc(m2) # here, for example adjusted ICC is 0.09, and unadjusted is 0.018 - after accounting for method and stage, only 9.4% of the remaining variation in gamete size is due to differences between specimens. This means: Most of the variation is within specimens – i.e., between developmental stages or due to measurement error. Specimens are fairly similar to each other once you account for stage and method. 

# Unadjusted ICC = the proportion of variance explained by the random effect without accounting for fixed effects (method and stage). The adjusted ICC accounts for fixed effects. Since method and stage explain a lot of variance, the adjusted ICC is higher (more variance is left for the random effect to explain after fixed effects are accounted for).


# ---- 11b. Phylum-specific ICC ----
icc_porifera <- performance::icc(
  lmer(feret_micron ~ method + stage + (1 | specimen_id),
       data = gametes %>% filter(phylum == "Porifera"))
)
print("ICC for Porifera:")
print(icc_porifera) # here: In sponges, 16.1% of the variation is between specimens. but here, we also have three species... 

icc_cnidaria <- performance::icc(
  lmer(feret_micron ~ method + stage + (1 | specimen_id),
       data = gametes %>% filter(phylum == "Cnidaria"))
)
print("ICC for Cnidaria:")
print(icc_cnidaria)

# ---- 11c. Overall ICC (all data) ----
icc_overall <- performance::icc(
  lmer(feret_micron ~ method + stage + (1 | specimen_id),
       data = gametes)
)
print("ICC for all data:")
print(icc_overall)

#Interpretation: Within each phylum, specimens are quite similar (low ICC). Between phyla, there is a large biological difference, which inflates the overall ICC. This supports the conclusion that most size variation is within specimens (stage differences) rather than between individuals.

```

## 13. FECUNDITY (SPONGES)

```{r fecundity}
# Using microCT data only
microct_data <- data %>% filter(method == "microCT")

gamete_counts <- microct_data %>%
  filter(grepl("Gamete", type, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(specimen_id) %>%
  summarise(n_gametes = n(), .groups = "drop")

tissue_volume <- microct_data %>%
  filter(type %in% c("Mesohyl", "Spicules")) %>%
  group_by(specimen_id) %>%
  summarise(tissue_volume = sum(volume, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

fecundity <- gamete_counts %>%
  left_join(tissue_volume, by = "specimen_id") %>%
  mutate(
    gamete_density = n_gametes / tissue_volume,
    gamete_density_log = log(gamete_density)
  )

print(fecundity)

# Optional fecundity plot (commented out)
ggplot(fecundity, aes(x = specimen_id, y = gamete_density)) +
geom_col() + labs(y = "Gamete density (per µm³)", x = "Specimen") + theme_bw()
```

```{r paragorgia-histogram}
# Load museum specimen data (additional microCT measurements)

  "specimen_id", "species_replicate", "phylum", "species", "stage",
  "type", "measurement", "volume", "surface_area_lindblad_2005_mm2",
  "aspect_ratio", "feret_min_mm", "feret_mean_mm", "feret_max_mm",
  "feret_micron", "notes", "annotation_method", "method"
)

# Subset Paragorgia microCT data from main dataset
paragorgia_microCT <- gametes[
  gametes$species == "Paragorgia arborea" &
  gametes$method == "microCT",
]

# Combine with museum data
paragorgia_all <- rbind(paragorgia_microCT, museum)

# Plot: density with stage-coloured rug
ggplot(paragorgia_all, aes(x = feret_micron)) +

  # Developmental stage zones (background shading)
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 400,  ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,

  annotate("rect", xmin = 400, xmax = 900, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,

  annotate("rect", xmin = 900, xmax = 2000, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#7570b3", alpha = 0.05) +

  geom_density(aes(fill = specimen_id), alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
```
